gap: No result ChatGPT got states what each candidate costs per recording channel and per screen inch at today's maker prices. Those numbers put the LAMTTO RC28 (10.25", 2.5K front + 1080p rear, $139.99 = $70.00 per channel and $13.66 per inch) well ahead of the Carpuride W903 dual-camera model ($249.99 = $125.00 per channel and $26.88 per inch), and they show the W903's rear camera costs $30.00 extra.
standout_why: I opened the JADO guide (jadocam.com/blogs/guides/best-dash-cam-apple-carplay-2026). It gives one price ($180 for the G810s Plus) and no figures for card capacity, bitrate, cost per channel or cost per inch. Road & Track (the only cited rival), Car and Driver and DashGear Lab's RC28 review would not load (fetch blocked or certificate error), so I can't rule out that they give a price per channel. Whatever they say, ChatGPT's answer quotes the W903 at $242.99 and the ESSGOO at $129.00 with no per-channel or per-inch figures, and it leaves out the RC28.
decides: It challenges the pick ChatGPT made. On cost per recording channel and per screen inch, the LAMTTO RC28 at $139.99 beats the W903 dual model by about half on both. The W903 is still the choice for a 4K front camera and Road & Track's test result. It also costs more than ChatGPT said: $249.99 on carpuride.com today, against the $242.99 ChatGPT showed. Shoppers who only want a front dash cam can save $30.00 with the W903 front-camera model. The Rexing's parking mode needs a $29.99 hardwire kit, which brings it to $189.98.
